newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share trade calm, not far off record highs.
newsitem.headline: German share trade calm, not far off record highs.

text.p: The German IBIS DAX index continued to trade within sight of record highs in post-bourse trade on Wednesday, but dealers said that dealings lacked much of the urgency of the previous week.

By 1348 GMT the IBIS DAX was up 44.82 points, a rise of 44.82 points or 1.02 percent, not far off a high of 4,449.33 points. The DAX index earlier ended bourse trade on a record high of 4,421.72 points, having risen 0.91 percent.
"The market is a lot quieter today. We had records in bourse trade, but few really noticed," a Frankfurt trader said.
Utility companies were in favour over the day, dealers said. "The favourites stocks are being rotated at the moment, which seem to be mainly driven by technical factors," a trader said.
Veba AG was up 1.65 marks at 103.45 marks, RWE AG was up 1.33 marks at 81.34 marks and Viag AG was up 11.10 marks at 787.90 marks.

Also in favour yet again was the banking sector, still riding high on merger mania as market players speculated about further mergers in the sector after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank said last week they would merge.
Vereinsbank was up 2.35 marks at 101.75 marks, while Hypo-Bank was up 1.25 marks at 77.50 marks.

Deutsche, which was holding an analysts' meeting after its H1 1997 results on Tuesday, was up 3.55 marks at 123.75 marks and Commerzbank advanced 96 pfennigs to 61.95 marks. Dresdner fell amid profit-taking.
